question: What do players think of Baldur's Gate 3's combat?
expected_answer: Very positively: players say the turn-based combat still feels fast and exciting, with bosses that pose interesting tactical challenges, and that it rewards creativity, since you can play smart, chaotic or stealthy and improvise when plans fail. It welcomes newcomers to D&D, because the interface shows your odds of success. The main frustration is the dice: an attack with a 95% chance of success can still miss at the worst moment, and newcomers find the frequent misses confusing at first, though many say it clicks after 20–30 hours. Some also find the early game frustrating on the default difficulty.

question: Is Hollow Knight good value for its price?
expected_answer: Yes, overwhelmingly: players call it insanely cheap for what it offers, around $15 for a huge world full of secrets, about 20 hours for a first playthrough and over 100 for completionists, plus free DLC added after release (such as Godhome). Several say paying full price is a way to support the small studio behind it.

question: What do players say about Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion?
expected_answer: Very positively: players say Phantom Liberty could stand on its own as a separate game, praising its story, characters, quests, atmosphere and its new district, Dogtown. Many link it to the 2.0 update released alongside it: together they turned a game with a disastrous launch into one that works and plays very well, and the DLC improves gameplay that had started to feel repetitive.

question: Is Red Dead Redemption 2 too slow-paced?
expected_answer: For most players, no: the slow pace is mentioned often, but usually as deliberate and part of the appeal, a slow-burning story that lets you get to know the characters and the world. The most common criticism is that the early chapters start slowly, though players say the story gets better as it unfolds. A minority find it tedious, with long animations and a lot of holding buttons, and say the game is not for them.

question: What do players think of Sekiro's parry-based combat?
expected_answer: Very positively: players call it one of the best combat systems they have played, built on a simple idea, deflecting attacks to break the enemy's posture, that feels brutal and unforgiving but also rhythmic, elegant and satisfying. It rewards aggressive play, with counters like the Mikiri Counter unlocked as you progress. The learning curve is steep, and players advise not giving up early. A minority finds the system too simple, mostly attacking and deflecting with lenient timing, and some attack patterns unfair.

question: Is Dying Light's co-op worth it?
expected_answer: Yes: players describe co-op as one of the most fun parts of the game, with friendly competitions (first to the airdrop, most loot, most kills) and chaotic, funny moments, with friends or with strangers online; a 2024 review says online co-op is still well populated. It is not required, though: players say the game is also great solo. Opinions are mixed on the separate 'Be the Zombie' mode, in which another player can invade your game as a powerful zombie: some find it fun, others say it offers little reason to play over standard co-op.

question: How well does God of War run on PC?
expected_answer: Very well for most players: they describe the PC port as excellent, well optimised and easy to run, with all the graphics options you could want, good keyboard and mouse controls, and native 4K and unlocked frame rates on powerful hardware. A few players report serious problems, especially on the Steam Deck: frame rate drops, crashes, freezes, screen tearing and audio issues.

question: Is Far Cry 6's story worth it, or is it more of the same?
expected_answer: Players are divided. The story is generally described as decent or okay rather than a reason to play, but the villain, Antón Castillo, stands out as memorable even for critical players. Some criticize the tone, which shifts from dark to goofy, and the large number of side characters. On the formula, many feel it is more of the same, with a repetitive open world and, for some, a downgrade from Far Cry 3 and 4; others consider it the best Far Cry in terms of gameplay mechanics, especially when bought on sale.

question: Has The Last of Us Part I's PC port improved since launch?
game: The Last of Us Part I
expected_answer: Partly. At launch, in March 2023, the port was widely criticized for frequent crashes, poor optimization and very high hardware requirements, and players advised waiting for patches. Later reviews are more mixed: some players in 2025 and 2026 describe smooth performance with no crashes, but others still report crashes, some apparently caused by memory leaks, and poor optimization more than a year after release. The port improved, but it was never fully fixed.

question: Does Borderlands 4 still have performance problems?
expected_answer: Yes: performance problems are reported from launch in September 2025 through the most recent reviews in late 2026, including long shader compilation at startup (often 10–15 minutes), stutters, crashes and very high hardware demands, with players saying that only a recent high-end PC, or upscaling and frame generation, gives smooth frame rates. Some players enjoy the game despite this and hope optimization will improve, but recent reviews do not describe the problems as fixed.

question: Did Fallout 4's next-gen update cause problems?
expected_answer: Yes, mainly for players who use mods. Long-time players say the 2024 next-gen update, and the later anniversary update, changed the game version, which broke the Script Extender (F4SE) and the mods that depend on it; some lost long save files or had to downgrade the game, and one describes it as far more crash-prone since the update. Some see this as pushing players toward Bethesda's paid Creation Club content. Others say the problems mostly affect modded installs and expect the modding community to adapt, as it did for Skyrim. Updates breaking F4SE is not new: players complained about the same problem with Creation Club updates in 2018.

question: How does Ghost of Tsushima run on the Steam Deck?
expected_answer: Very well, according to the small number of reviews from Steam Deck players: they describe it as very well optimized and smooth, with no lag and great visuals from start to finish, including the Iki Island expansion. question: How does Lies of P compare to Sekiro and other FromSoftware games?
expected_answer: Very favorably: players often call it one of the best soulslikes made outside FromSoftware, with polish and level design that other FromSoftware imitators rarely achieve. Its combat is described as Bloodborne with some Sekiro, combining Bloodborne's rally (attacking back to recover health) with Sekiro-style perfect blocks that break enemy posture. Some prefer it to recent FromSoftware games, praising its clearer storytelling and fewer frustrating design choices; others feel it stays too close to Bloodborne, or that mixing the two systems makes combat annoying, with weaker dodging than in FromSoftware's games.

question: Do players think Cyberpunk 2077 is better than The Witcher 3?
expected_answer: Players are split, and the answer depends on when they played. At its 2020 launch, Cyberpunk disappointed many players who knew CD Projekt Red from The Witcher series, because it was overpromised and released unfinished, although some said its side quests matched The Witcher 3's. After the 2.0 update and Phantom Liberty in 2023, several Witcher fans say Cyberpunk matches or even surpasses The Witcher 3, especially for its story and characters, while others, even after the patches, still rank The Witcher 3 first.

question: How does Assassin's Creed Shadows compare to Ghost of Tsushima?
expected_answer: Most players who compare them prefer Ghost of Tsushima, for its smoother, more grounded combat, better world design, and better story and visual style; even players who enjoy Shadows concede this. Shadows is still recommended as a good follow-up for fans of feudal Japan, with stealth as Naoe praised as the best in the series and fun, powerful combat as Yasuke. Critics add that it follows the familiar Assassin's Creed formula and pushes microtransactions.

question: What are the main complaints about Hollow Knight?
expected_answer: Complaints are few, and they mostly come from players who still recommend the game. The recurring ones are: the difficulty, with some bosses, including the final boss, criticized as unfair for relying on projectiles or reacting too quickly to the player's inputs; the lack of guidance, which can make exploration overwhelming or frustrating for players who prefer linear games; backtracking across the large map after unlocking new abilities, with long walks between benches, including the walk back to recover what you lost after dying; and spells sharing the same resource as healing, so they are rarely used.

question: What do players think of 007 First Light's gameplay?
expected_answer: Mostly positive. Players say the gadgets, gunplay and stealth all 'feel very Bond', and some call it the best Bond game; they praise the Q-Watch gadgets (hacking, remote control, traps, tranquilizers), mechanics taught naturally through the story, and missions that can be approached by sneaking, bluffing past guards, playing non-lethally or going in loud. The recurring criticism is that it is linear and cinematic: critics say the freedom of approach is mostly an illusion, gadgets are either useless or overpowered and limited by battery, it relies heavily on cutscenes, and it falls off after a strong first half. Players sum it up as playing a Bond movie: great for Bond fans, less so for players looking for exploration.

question: Is the story of The Last of Us Part I worth it, even with the bad PC reviews?
game: The Last of Us Part I
expected_answer: Yes: players, including many who left negative reviews, call the story one of the best in gaming, a masterclass in character development driven by the relationship between Joel and Ellie, with excellent acting and serious themes. Two caveats: the story is linear, so you follow the characters rather than shape the story, and a few find the premise itself familiar, crediting the characters rather than the plot.
